# Intake Brief — Insert selected work-item ID into herdr command input forms (WL-0MSGPSEFW006VINF)

## Problem statement

When typing a free-form prompt in a herdr command input form (e.g. the `P-p` chord, which opens a prompt sent to a new Pi agent pane), there is no discoverable way to reference the currently selected work item by its ID. The `<id>` magic token already works inside form field values (both chord and single-key form paths in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` resolve it to the selected item's ID on submit), but the behavior is undocumented, untested, and invisible in the UI — and in one edge case (no item selected, `P-p` path) a literal `<id>` leaks through to Pi.

## Users

- **Herdr users** who open the `P-p` free-form prompt (or any chord form) and want the prompt to reference the work item they currently have selected — without memorising/pasting the ID.
- **Pi agents / operators** who receive the prompt — the prompt becomes self-contained with the item ID, so no follow-up lookup is needed.

User stories:
- As a Herdr user with an item selected in the worklist, I want to type `<id>` in the `P-p` free-form prompt so the selected item's ID is inserted into the prompt sent to Pi.
- As a Herdr user filling any chord command form (e.g. `u-t` title, `u-s` stage), I want `<id>` to resolve to the currently selected item's ID the same way it does in command templates.
- As a new Herdr user, I want the form dialog to hint that `<id>` is available, so I don't need to read the README to discover it.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Typing `<id>` in the `P-p` free-form prompt field inserts the currently selected work item's ID into the prompt text sent to Pi (verified by an automated regression test on the form-submit path; no new `wl` spawn needed).
2. The same `<id>`-in-field behavior works in **all** herdr command input forms, for both the chord and single-key dispatch paths.
3. The form dialog renders a discoverability hint (e.g. a footer/help line such as "type `<id>` to insert the selected item's ID") whenever the form is shown.
4. When no work item is selected and a form field value contains `<id>`, the behavior is graceful and consistent across all paths — no literal `<id>` is sent to Pi; the documented decision (see Risks & assumptions) is implemented and covered by a test.
5. `packages/herdr/README.md` documents the `<id>`-in-form-field behavior, including the `P-p` free-prompt example.
6. Full project test suite passes with the new changes; new tests cover the free-prompt case, the generic form case, the no-item-selected edge case, and the discoverability hint.

## Constraints

- **No change to `<id>` handling in command templates** — the existing `KNOWN_IDENTIFIERS` / `substituteIdentifiers` mechanism in `packages/herdr/src/form-dialog.ts` stays as-is.
- **No changes to the chord definitions** in `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` (P-p, P-a, u-*, etc. remain bound exactly as today).
- No modal/UX overhaul of the form dialog — the hint is a minimal addition to the existing form render.
- All work tracked in wl; no changes to work-item tracking tooling.

## Existing state

- `P-p` chord → `/prompt:<prompt>` opens the command input form (`FormState` in `packages/herdr/src/form-dialog.ts`); on submit the resulting command routes through `worklist.ts` and spawns a Pi agent pane with the bare prompt text (`stripAgentPromptPrefix` in `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`).
- `KNOWN_IDENTIFIERS = {'id'}` in `form-dialog.ts` — `<id>` never triggers an unknown-identifier prompt; `substituteIdentifiers` leaves `<id>` intact in field values.
- Both form onSubmit callbacks in `worklist.ts` (chord-complete path ~line 2353 and single-key path ~line 2464) replace `<id>` with the selected item's ID via `flat[idx].id`.
- No regression test covers `<id>` typed inside a form field value; no UI hint; README documents `<id>` resolution for command templates only, not for field values/free prompts.
- Edge case: in the form paths, when no item is selected and the field value contains `<id>`, `finalCmd` keeps the literal `<id>` and it is sent (visible to Pi in the `P-p` case); the non-form `executeResolvedCommand` path instead returns a graceful `noop` when `<id>` is in the command and nothing is selected — inconsistent.

## Desired change

- **Verify + formalise the existing mechanism**: add regression tests asserting `<id>` in a form field value resolves to the selected item's ID, for the free prompt (P-p) and generic forms, across chord and single-key paths.
- **Discoverability**: render a hint line in the form dialog ("type `<id>` to insert the selected item's ID") and document the behavior in `packages/herdr/README.md` (including the `P-p` free-prompt example).
- **Graceful no-item-selected handling**: decide and implement one consistent behavior for `<id>` in field values when nothing is selected (proposed: drop the command with a toast, matching the existing `noop` convention for template `<id>`; documented in the work item).
- **No new mechanism** — the magic-token approach was chosen in intake (option a); chord-based insertion and pre-filled prompts were considered and explicitly out of scope.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/form-dialog.ts` — render the `<id>` discoverability hint in the form dialog (footer/help line); unchanged substitution logic.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — the two form onSubmit callbacks: consistent no-item-selected handling (drop + toast); no change to existing `<id>` resolution.
- `packages/herdr/src/form-dialog.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — regression tests for `<id>`-in-field resolution, the no-item-selected edge case, and the hint rendering.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — document `<id>` inside form field values / free prompts.

## Related work

- **Herdr shortcuts: P-p free prompt and P-a audit-gaps prompt (WL-0MSGHNTMF000YKRI)** — completed; introduced the `P-p` chord this feature builds on.
- **Herdr plugin: free-form prompt shortcut opens new pi pane (WL-0MSC0O8HN000EBFH)** — completed; `/prompt:` routing + `send-to-pi.sh` pane spawning.
- **Form input dialog for unknown identifiers in Herdr chord commands (WL-0MS690SJG003H7WK)** — completed; introduced `FormState` / form-dialog.
- **Shortcuts with multiple <id> tokens only replace the first occurrence (WL-0MRNLF5UO0088ID2)** — completed; multiple-`<id>` handling relevant to the `u-t`/`u-s` edge case.
- **Wire text-insertion template commands (WL-0MS4GIMBD008GWVM)** — completed; text-insertion template wiring in the same code area.
- **Related work (automated report, /skill:find-related)** — additional matches retained as lower-priority context: **wl sync timeouts (WL-0MSAKM838006RZNR)** (completed; herdr auto-sync spawn/timeout context), **[test-failure] send-to-pi.sh / open-pi-agent.sh pane-launch tests (WL-0MSGAKL8R009GB1X)** (completed; pane-launch regression relevant to the P-p spawn path), **Unify dialog widget construction and layout helpers (WL-0MNX4D4G8009XZNJ)** (completed; form-dialog rendering helpers). Automated repo-file matches (audit_runner.py, intake SKILL.md) were reviewed and dropped — generic keyword noise from the wrong repo root.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Over-implementation risk:** the mechanism already exists; the main risk is building a redundant insertion mechanism instead of testing + surfacing the existing magic token. Mitigation: scope is verification, discoverability, and edge-case handling only.
- **No-item-selected edge case:** proposed default = drop the command with a toast (consistent with template `<id>` noop convention). Assumption: users prefer a clear "no item selected" signal over sending a literal `<id>` to Pi.
- **Multi-`<id>` forms (`u-t` title, `u-s` stage):** typing `<id>` into such a field replaces every `<id>` in the command (target and field value) with the selected ID — existing multiple-`<id>` behavior, accepted as-is; noted in docs.
- **Scope-creep risk:** chord-based insertion and pre-filled prompts (intake options b/c) are out of scope; if requested later, record as linked work items rather than expanding this one.
- **Assumption:** the selected item is the one highlighted in the herdr worklist (`state.selectedIndex`), same source used by all existing `<id>` substitutions.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "The `WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3` reference — that ID is an existing, unrelated in-progress work item (the wl read-cache epic). Which did you mean? (a) It was simply the item currently selected in your herdr pane — the feature is generic: insert *whatever* item is currently selected. (b) It should be a magic token: typing that literal string into the prompt gets replaced with the currently selected item's ID before sending. (c) Something else." — Answer (operator): "a" — generic; insert whatever item is currently selected. Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "Insertion mechanism — how should the ID get into the input box while typing? (a) A magic token in the prompt text (e.g. typing `<id>` — consistent with the existing placeholder convention in herdr commands). (b) A chord/keypress *inside* the input box (e.g. a key or chord that pastes the selected ID at the cursor). (c) Open the P-p prompt pre-filled with the selected ID. (d) Freeform." — Answer (operator): "a" — magic token (`<id>`). Source: interactive reply. Note: (b) and (c) explicitly out of scope.
- Q3: "Scope — which input boxes should support this? (a) Only the herdr P-p free-prompt input box. (b) All herdr command input forms. (c) Also the main pi prompt input (the `P` key in the pi TUI) — note: that lives in pi core and may not be reachable from a herdr plugin extension." — Answer (operator): "b" — all herdr command input forms. Source: interactive reply. Note: pi core input out of scope.
- Q4 (agent research note, no user answer required): does typing `<id>` in a form field already work? — Research: inspected `form-dialog.ts` (`KNOWN_IDENTIFIERS`, `substituteIdentifiers`) and both onSubmit callbacks in `worklist.ts`; the mechanism already resolves `<id>` to the selected item's ID on submit in both chord and single-key paths. No test covers this path; no UI hint; `P-p` with no item selected leaks literal `<id>` to Pi. Findings incorporated into Existing state / Desired change.

# Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

## Summary
Read the plugin version at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` and render it as a dimmed, right-aligned `v<version>` suffix in the work item selection list header, without disturbing the left-aligned title.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A runtime helper reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (JSON parse via `readFileSync`, following the `shortcut-config.ts` pattern); when the file is missing or unparseable it falls back gracefully (e.g. `'?'` or omit) without throwing.
- The list-mode header renders `v<version>` right-aligned to `cols` (visible-width padding computed with ANSI codes stripped before padding), dimmed via `ANSI.dim`, matching the `[auto-refresh on]` treatment; the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title is unchanged.
- The version is read at runtime from the manifest, not hardcoded in the renderer (stays in sync with the manifest version).
- On narrow panes where the suffix would overlap the title, the suffix is dropped or truncated (guard on `cols`) — no layout breakage, no overflow beyond the pane width.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes, including the header version tests (F1).

## Minimal Implementation
- Add a small version-read helper in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (or a sibling module) using the `readFileSync`/`dirname` pattern from `shortcut-config.ts`, with a safe fallback.
- In the list-mode header renderer (near line ~1585): compute the header's visible width, pad to `cols`, and append the dimmed `v<version>` suffix right-aligned; reuse `truncateLine`/visible-length logic; guard on `cols` for narrow panes.
- Keep the renderer testable via the existing `readFile`-style injection seam where practical.

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: header version rendering tests (F1) — test-first ordering.

## Deliverables
- Updated `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; version helper; no change to `packages/herdr/package.json` (version source only).
data.title: Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

# Canonical test suite excludes 77 root-level tests/*.test.ts files

> **Planning review (plan skill, 2026-10-25).** Counts and risks below were verified against the `dev` tree. Corrected facts are marked **[verified]**; no new requirements were invented — the one scope question beyond `tests/` is recorded as an OPEN QUESTION in the Appendix.

## Problem Statement

`.pi/test-config.json` declares the canonical suite as `npm --silent test -- tests/cli` + `npm --silent test -- tests/unit`. Vitest therefore runs 160 of the 277 test files under `tests/` (111 in `tests/cli`, 49 in `tests/unit`). The **77** root-level `tests/*.test.ts` files (`tests/read-cache.test.ts`, `tests/read-cache-cli.test.ts`, `tests/spawn-counter.test.ts`, `tests/audit.test.ts`, …) are never executed by any *full-suite* gate: `/skill:test --type full`, the ship release gate, or an audit F3 auto-run. `implement.py finish` (changed scope) can run a root-level file, but only when that file is itself affected by the diff — nothing runs them as part of the declared full suite.

**[verified] The gap is wider than the root level.** 117 `tests/` files are outside the canonical suite today:

| Location | Files | In canonical suite? |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/` (root level) | 77 | No |
| `tests/cli` | 111 | Yes |
| `tests/unit` | 49 | Yes |
| `tests/bench` | 4 | No |
| `tests/debug` | 1 | No |
| `tests/extensions` | 1 | No |
| `tests/herdr` | 20 | No |
| `tests/integration` | 5 | No |
| `tests/lib` | 6 | No |
| `tests/scripts` | 3 | No |
| **`tests/` total** | **277** | **160 (58 %)** |

## Goal

The canonical full suite executes every test file, or each exclusion is documented with a rationale.

## Users / Stakeholders

- **Agent tiers** (implement, audit, test): rely on the canonical full suite for gate enforcement.
- **Producer**: needs the canonical suite to be a reliable proxy for repo health.
- **CI**: uses `npm test` (the whole vitest suite, 277 `tests/` + 162 `packages/` files) — the canonical subset is not a reliable proxy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The canonical suite command(s) in `.pi/test-config.json` cover root-level `tests/*.test.ts` files, or each exclusion is documented with a reason.
- A full `/skill:test` run reports the root-level files as executed (currently 0 of 77).
- Root-level failures surfaced by the change are triaged into `test-failure` work items.
- Documented in `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` (the “Test gates” section, which states it is shared with this item) so work items cannot claim coverage the gate does not provide — including the final coverage table (files executed / files excluded / why) and the measured runtime.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Runtime budget:** the existing canonical suite takes ~305 s (`tests/cli` ≈ 181–430 s depending on host load + `tests/unit` ≈ 7 s). The 77 root-level files add an unknown cost; the wider `tests/` umbrella adds the 40 files above. Runtime **must** be measured before and after with the test-skill runner (`run_tests.py`, which records cache evidence) — not with an ad-hoc `npx vitest`, and not by an agent invoking vitest directly.
- **[verified] Evidence-path constraint:** the audit’s full-suite evidence resolves `--type full` from `suiteCommands` only; a new named `groups.*` entry does **not** count as full-suite evidence (`docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` → “Cache evidence scope”). The fix must therefore land in `suiteCommands` (extend or replace), not only in a named group.
- **[verified] Vitest filter mechanics:** `npm test` maps to `vitest run`, and positional arguments are **substring** filters on the path relative to the repo root (`vitest/dist/chunks/cli-api.*.js` → `filterFiles()` → `testFile.includes(filter)`). There is no depth, negation or regex support, so:
  - `npm --silent test -- tests` selects all 277 `tests/` files (and nothing outside `tests/` — no other `.test.ts` path contains the substring `tests`),
  - there is **no** positional filter that selects root-level files only.
  Two viable designs follow: (a) replace the two narrow commands with the single umbrella `npm --silent test -- tests`; or (b) keep them and add a dedicated vitest config (e.g. `vitest.tests-root.config.ts` with `include: ['tests/*.test.ts']`) invoked via `--config`. Option (a) also closes the 40-file gap for free and cannot double-execute because a single vitest run de-duplicates its own file set.
- **[verified] Overlapping basenames are intentional variants, not duplicates:** `audit.test.ts`, `doctor-foreign-items-apply.test.ts`, `process-lifecycle.test.ts`, `sync-author-gate.test.ts` exist at both root and `tests/cli/`, but the root copies are unit-level (import `src/*.js`, e.g. 38-line `tests/audit.test.ts`) while the `tests/cli` copies are CLI/integration-level (e.g. 41-line `tests/cli/audit.test.ts`; `tests/process-lifecycle.test.ts` 401 lines vs `tests/cli/process-lifecycle.test.ts` 292 lines). **Both must execute.** The only risk is double execution, which design (a) avoids.
- **Vitest configuration:** `vitest.config.ts` discovers all test files by default (`pool: 'forks'`, `isolate: true`, `singleFork: true`, `maxWorkers: 4`, worktree exclusions). Any new command must keep those settings; do not add a second `include` that drops the worktree/`node_modules` excludes.
- **[verified] Related sibling is closed won't-fix:** WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8 (herdr package tests) was closed by producer decision — the herdr package suite stays out of the canonical suite. The `groups.herdr` entry now in `.pi/test-config.json` came from WL-0MVH751AJ009R4SN, and `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` records the sanctioned exclusion. Nothing to coordinate, but do **not** re-litigate that decision, and do **not** assume “full parity with `npm test`” is the accepted intent.

## Existing State

- `.pi/test-config.json`: `suiteCommands` = `tests/cli` (111 files) + `tests/unit` (49 files) = 160 files; `groups.herdr` = `packages/herdr/src` (opt-in, cache-recorded); `timeoutPerCommand: 1800`.
- `.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json`: type map defines only `herdr`; `--type full` resolves from `suiteCommands`, so extending `suiteCommands` is sufficient — no extension change needed.
- `vitest.config.ts`: default include discovers 277 `tests/` + 162 `packages/` test files; gates narrow to the canonical subset.
- 117 `tests/` files are never executed by a full-suite gate (77 root-level + 40 in `bench/`, `debug/`, `extensions/`, `herdr/`, `integration/`, `lib/`, `scripts/`).
- 4 basenames exist at both root and `tests/cli/` (intentional unit vs CLI variants — both must run).
- The legacy root `test/` directory no longer exists (the baseline doc’s `test/` row is stale — fix while updating it).
- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` has a “Test gates” section that explicitly says it is shared with this item: “extend this section rather than adding a second one”.
- The `pre-push` hook does not run the test suite at all (branch policy, context budget, `wl sync` only) — do not claim push-time coverage.

## Desired Change

1. Extend (or replace) `suiteCommands` in `.pi/test-config.json` so a `--type full` run executes the root-level files. Preferred: a single `npm --silent test -- tests` (covers all 277 `tests/` files, no double execution). Fallback: keep the two existing commands and add a root-only vitest config invoked with `--config`, then document the 40 remaining unexecuted files with a rationale (AC1).
2. Verify executed-file count against the 277-file expectation (vitest’s reported “Test Files N passed” plus a diff of executed vs expected paths) and confirm no file runs twice.
3. Measure runtime before/after via `run_tests.py` and record both numbers.
4. Update `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md`: extend the existing “Test gates” section with the new commands, the coverage table (executed / excluded / why), the measured runtime, and the stale legacy `test/` row.
5. Triage any newly surfaced failures into `test-failure` items (AC3) — do not let triage block the config change, and do not leave failures un-triaged.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.pi/test-config.json` — extend/replace `suiteCommands` (keep `groups` intact)
- `vitest.config.ts` — only if the root-only config approach is chosen; keep `pool`/`isolate`/`singleFork` and the worktree exclusions
- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` — extend the “Test gates” section; fix the stale legacy `test/` row
- `tests/audit.test.ts` — one of the 4 shared-basename variants that must execute alongside `tests/cli/audit.test.ts`
- `.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json` — inspect only (no change expected: `--type full` reads `suiteCommands`)

## Risks & Assumptions

- ~~4 overlapping files may be duplicates~~ **[verified] they are intentional unit-vs-CLI variants; both must execute.** Residual risk is only double execution — avoided by the single umbrella command, and checkable by comparing executed-file count with the 277 expectation.
- **Runtime growth unknown** — these files are never run today; the budget may grow beyond ~305 s. Measure before/after; if a file is pathologically slow, document the *reason* (exclusion rationale) rather than silently excluding it.
- **Hidden failures** — the 117 files may already be red; surfacing them creates triage work (AC3 requires triage, not a blocking gate).
- ~~Sibling fix may not have landed~~ **[verified] the sibling was closed won't-fix**, and `groups.herdr` exists from WL-0MVH751AJ009R4SN; the herdr exclusion is producer-sanctioned and documented.
- **Assumption (corrected):** the accepted intent is “every test file is covered by the canonical suite, or has an explicit documented exclusion” — **not** full parity with `npm test`, because packages/herdr is deliberately excluded.
- **Out of `tests/` scope (see OPEN QUESTION):** `packages/` holds 162 test files, of which only `packages/herdr/src` (107, excluded by decision) is referenced at all; `packages/tui/extensions` (22) is referenced by neither `suiteCommands` nor any group.

## Related Work

- **WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8** — Canonical full suite excludes herdr package tests (same root cause, different scope; **closed won't-fix** by producer decision — the exclusion is intentional)
- **WL-0MVH751AJ009R4SN** — added `groups.herdr` to `.pi/test-config.json` (the pattern to keep intact)
- **WL-0MVGJ4WSS005BMSI** / **WL-0MVH75NY3002TTX9** — author of the shared “Test gates / Canonical gate reference” section in `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md`
- **WL-0MVFRRGGC001IQK1** — F8 cache-prune tests (discoverer — references `tests/read-cache.test.ts` / `tests/read-cache-cli.test.ts`, which are in the excluded set)
- **WL-0MVNUHWH500196K1** — herdr local-preference default flip; source of the additional-gap comment (`tests/herdr/**`, `packages/tui/extensions/**`)
- **WL-0MSKSMM5E002O35Q** — Audit auto-green-run: `NODE_SUITE_DIRS` includes non-existent `tests/node` (completed — same theme of gate paths vs on-disk layout)
- **`docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md`** — documents the canonical suite as a subset of the full vitest suite
- Automated find-related report appended to the item by the find-related skill (completed items WL-0MQDR5ICN0098ID6, WL-0MSKSMM5E002O35Q, WL-0MULP57FU0051N43).

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

### Planning review (2026-10-25, plan skill)

No producer interview was required — the item is small (effort Small / risk Low, below the planning threshold), so planning ran the six automated review stages against the existing content instead of decomposing it.

Corrections applied during the review (all evidence-backed):

- Q: “How many root-level files are actually excluded — the item says 76?” Answer (repo evidence, `git ls-files | grep -E '^tests/[^/]+\.test\.ts$' | wc -l` → 77): **77** at the current `dev` tree; the title and AC2 were corrected. One file was added to `tests/` since the item was filed.
- Q: “Are the 4 shared basenames duplicates?” Answer (repo evidence, `diff tests/<f> tests/cli/<f>` on all four): **No** — all four differ, and the doc comments read “Unit tests for …” (root) vs “CLI tests for …” (`tests/cli`). Both variants must execute.
- Q: “Did the herdr sibling fix land, and does its decision still hold?” Answer (`wl show WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8`): the item was closed **won't-fix** by producer decision; `groups.herdr` was added separately by WL-0MVH751AJ009R4SN. Recorded above so the implementer does not re-open it.
- Q: “Can a vitest positional filter select only root-level files?” Answer (repo evidence, `node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/cli-api.*.js` → `filterFiles()`): **No** — filters are plain substring matches on the relative path. Design options recorded under Constraints.

**OPEN QUESTION (for the producer — does not block this item).** The additional-gap comment (WL-0MVNUHWH500196K1, author `implement`) notes that `packages/tui/extensions/**` (22 test files) is covered by neither `suiteCommands` nor any group, and `tests/herdr/**` (20 files) is likewise uncovered. The `tests/herdr/` part is closed by this item’s `tests/` umbrella fix; the `packages/tui/extensions` part is not. *Why it matters:* leaving it out keeps a documented gap between the gate and CI. *Recommended option:* file a separate `discovered-from:WL-0MVG4FF9200346NR` item for `packages/` non-herdr coverage, keeping this item’s scope to `tests/` and its Small effort estimate intact. Alternative options: (a) fold `packages/tui/extensions/**` into this item (raises effort/risk — re-estimate), or (b) record it as an accepted, documented exclusion in `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` when writing the coverage table.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items

# Pi extension not showing work item title (WL-0MVGB23MM004X501)

## Problem statement

The Worklog Pi extension's footer shows the work item **ID** but silently omits the
**title** for some work items. The title is never displayed even though the
raw command text is shown, so the footer lacks the at-a-glance identification the
feature was built for (WL-0MQLG8PK80041FM3 / WL-0MQLJU82A000AT2W).

## Users

- **Pi TUI users** running Worklog skills with a work item ID.
  - *As a developer running `/intake RISE-0MVCFSM9B0019M8L`, I want the footer to
    show `intake RISE-0MVCFSM9B0019M8L AI cards should be face down` so I can
    confirm which item the agent is working on without scrolling the transcript.*
- **Herdr downtime workers** that auto-dispatch `/skill:intake` on cross-project
  items; their panes surface the same footer.

## Observed behaviour

- Footer always shows the work item ID.
- The title suffix is missing for *some* items only — the same command against a
  local project item shows both ID and title.
- Reproduced example from the report: `/intake RISE-0MVCFSM9B0019M8L`.

## Root-cause analysis (performed during intake)

Two independent failure modes share one symptom. Both are in the title-resolution
path used by the extension and are silent by design (the feature spec requires
graceful fallback with no error shown).

1. **Cross-project IDs are not resolved (primary).** Both title-resolution call
   sites spawn the CLI as `wl show <id> --json` with **cwd only**:
   - `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/activity-indicator.ts` →
     `resolveWorkItemTitle()` → `runWl('show', [id], { timeout: 2000 })`
   - `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/session-health.ts` → `startTicker()` →
     `runWl('show', [wlId], { timeout: 2000 })`

   `runWl` (`packages/tui/extensions/wl-integration.ts`) forwards to
   `runWlCommand` (`src/wl-integration/spawn.ts`), which spawns `wl` in
   `process.cwd()` and never passes `--worklog-dir`. Verified evidence:

   ```
   $ cd /home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub && wl show RISE-0MVCFSM9B0019M8L --json
   {"success": false, "error": "Work item not found: RISE-0MVCFSM9B0019M8L"}

   $ cd /home/rgardler/projects/tce-the-rising && wl show RISE-0MVCFSM9B0019M8L --json
   {"success": true, "workItem": {"id": "RISE-0MVCFSM9B0019M8L", "title": "AI cards should be face down", ...}}
   ```

   The skills layer *does* handle this — `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`
   resolves `--worklog-dir` via a **prefix-to-sibling scan**
   (`SIBLING_SCAN_ROOT/*/.worklog/config.yaml`, `prefix: RISE` →
   `/home/rgardler/projects/tce-the-rising/.worklog`). The extension has no
   equivalent, so any ID whose prefix belongs to a sibling project silently
   falls back to raw text. A git-history scan (`git log -S "worklog-dir" --
   packages/tui/extensions/wl-integration.ts`) shows this gap is long-standing,
   not a recent regression — the feature only *appears* to "have stopped"
   working because cross-project work is now routine.

2. **The 2 s timeout is marginal for large items (secondary).** Measured on the
   reported example: cold run **2.36 s**, warm runs 1.10–1.29 s against an 18 KB
   JSON payload (full description). Local medium-size items measured
   1.15–1.29 s. Under machine load (concurrent agents/tests) a warm lookup can
   cross the 2 000 ms ceiling, so the same item can intermittently lose its
   title. This also explains the "doesn't always happen" phrasing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** When the footer resolves a work item ID that lives in a **sibling project's**
   worklog (e.g. `RISE-…` while the session cwd is ContextHub), the footer shows
   the command, the ID, and the resolved title — verified against the reported
   reproduction (`RISE-0MVCFSM9B0019M8L` → `AI cards should be face down`).
- **AC2:** Title resolution uses the same prefix-to-sibling worklog resolution that the
   skills layer already uses (`prefix: <PFX>` in `SIBLING_SCAN_ROOT/*/.worklog/config.yaml`),
   falling back to cwd when no sibling matches — no new resolution algorithm is
   invented.
- **AC3:** The same fix applies to **both** call sites: the activity-indicator status
   line (`activity-indicator.ts`) and the footer's initial-prompt preview
   (`session-health.ts`); a single shared resolver is used so they cannot drift.
- **AC4:** The lookup timeout is raised (or the lookup made demonstrably fast enough)
   so that a large work item's title resolves reliably on a loaded machine; a
   regression test pins the timeout budget and a measured cold-start lookup for
   a >15 KB item succeeds.
- **AC5:** Lookup failure still degrades silently to the raw text, displaying no error
   (preserves AC 3 of WL-0MQLG8PK80041FM3).
- **AC6:** No new subprocess is spawned per keystroke/tick: sibling-prefix resolution is
   memoised per process (matching the memoised scan in `status_lifecycle.py`), so
   the per-tick footer refresh does not repeatedly scan the filesystem.
- **AC7:** Regression tests cover: cross-project resolution success, unresolvable ID
   fallback, non-TUI mode degradation, and both call sites sharing the resolver.
- **AC8:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **AC9:** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No change to `wl` CLI behaviour; the fix must live in the extension layer.
- `wl-integration.ts` must keep its existing `runWl(command, args, options)`
  signature working for all other callers (browse/lease/recovery modules).
- Prefix-to-sibling resolution must not shell out; read `.worklog/config.yaml`
  files directly, mirroring `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`
  (`_find_worklog_dir_by_prefix`).
- Must degrade gracefully when `SIBLING_SCAN_ROOT` does not exist or a project's
  `config.yaml` is malformed (skip that project).
- Windows/portable: use `path` APIs, no shell globbing.
- Work item IDs follow `<PREFIX>-<HASH>` with a 2–3 letter uppercase prefix;
  the existing `WORK_ITEM_ID_REGEX` stays unchanged.
- **Ambiguous prefixes (added during plan review):** sibling prefixes are not
  unique — verified on this machine, `POD` is shared by 12 `podcast-*` projects
  under `SIBLING_SCAN_ROOT`. The reference scan (`_find_worklog_dir_by_prefix`)
  returns the first match in sorted order, so prefix-only resolution can point
  at a sibling that does **not** own the item. The extension resolver must never
  return a worklog dir that does not own the ID; showing no title is acceptable,
  showing another project's title (or a "not found") is not. The tie-break
  policy is recorded as an OPEN QUESTION in the Appendix.

## Existing state

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/activity-indicator.ts` — `resolveWorkItemTitle()`
  calls `runWl('show', [id], { timeout: 2000 })` with no worklog dir;
  `showActivityWithTitleLookup()` composes `${commandCtx} ${truncateWorkItemId(id)} ${title}`.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/session-health.ts` — `startTicker().refreshState()`
  enriches `state.initialPrompt` with the same `runWl('show', …, { timeout: 2000 })` call.
- `packages/tui/extensions/wl-integration.ts` — thin `runWl` wrapper that forwards
  `cwd`/`timeout` to `runWlCommand`; no worklog-dir awareness.
- `src/wl-integration/spawn.ts` — `runWlCommand(cmdArgs, { timeoutMs, cwd, env })`
  spawns `wl` in `cwd` with a default 15 s timeout and `maxBuffer` 20 MB.
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — reference implementation of
  prefix-to-sibling resolution (`SIBLING_SCAN_ROOT`, `_find_worklog_dir_by_prefix`,
  `functools.cache`-memoised).
- `tests/verify-blessed-removal.test.ts` only asserts the file exists; the
  original `activity-indicator.test.ts` was deleted in commit `386ba9a2`
  (WL-0MSGI7PV9004UD0N), so there is currently **no behavioural test** covering
  title resolution.

## Desired change

**Test-first ordering:** the behavioural tests in step 5 (resolver unit tests plus
restored `activity-indicator`/`session-health` coverage) are written first and
observed failing; each of steps 1–4 lands only with its tests green.

1. Add a shared, memoised worklog-dir resolver in the extension layer
   (e.g. `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/worklog-dir.ts`) that:
   - extracts the ID prefix (`^[A-Z]{2,3}-`),
   - scans `<SIBLING_SCAN_ROOT>/*/.worklog/config.yaml` for a matching `prefix:`,
   - caches the prefix→dir mapping for the process lifetime,
   - returns `null` when nothing matches (caller then falls back to cwd).
2. Extend `runWl` (or a dedicated `runWlForWorkItem`) to append
   `--worklog-dir <resolved>` when the command's args contain a work item ID.
3. Route both title-resolution call sites through that single helper; remove the
   duplicated `runWl('show', …)` blocks.
4. Raise the lookup budget (e.g. 5 s) *and* verify latency headroom in a test, so
   the footer still degrades gracefully but no longer times out on a large item
   on a warm DB.
5. Reinstate behavioural tests for `detectWorkItemId`, `formatCommandContext`,
   cross-project resolution, fallback-on-failure, and the shared resolver's
   memoisation.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/worklog-dir.ts` (new) — memoised
  prefix-to-sibling worklog-dir resolver (ported from `status_lifecycle.py`).
- `packages/tui/extensions/wl-integration.ts` — inject `--worklog-dir` for
  work-item-scoped commands; export the resolver for reuse.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/activity-indicator.ts` — use the shared
  resolver/helper in `resolveWorkItemTitle`; raise the timeout.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/session-health.ts` — same helper in
  `refreshState()`; delete the duplicated enrichment block.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/worklog-dir.test.ts` (new) — resolver:
  prefix hit, prefix miss, missing scan root, malformed config, memoisation.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/activity-indicator.test.ts` (restored) —
  title resolution, cross-project path, fallback, non-TUI degradation.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/session-health.test.ts` — initial-prompt
  enrichment uses the shared resolver.
- `tests/unit/wl-integration.test.ts` — existing `runWl`/`runWlCommand` tests;
  extend with `--worklog-dir` injection (sibling hit, no hit, existing
  `runWl(command, args, options)` signature unchanged for other callers).
- `src/wl-integration/spawn.ts` — reference only; the constraint is no CLI/spawn
  behaviour change, so the injected flag must arrive as a plain `wl` argument.
- `README.md` / extension docs — note that cross-project IDs resolve via the
  sibling scan.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** `SIBLING_SCAN_ROOT` for the extension is the parent of the repo
  root (`/home/rgardler/projects`), matching `status_lifecycle.REPO_ROOT.parent`.
  The extension must derive it from its own installed location, not from
  `process.cwd()`; when it cannot be derived, resolution falls back to cwd
  (today's behaviour) rather than throwing.
- **Assumption:** the reported "footer" means both the line-1 activity status and
  the line-3 initial-prompt preview; the intake fix covers both since they share
  the same broken lookup.
- **Risk — starting a regression for in-repo IDs.** Passing `--worklog-dir`
  unconditionally could break worktree sessions, where `.worklog/` holds only a
  committed `config.yaml`. Mitigation: only pass the flag when a sibling prefix
  match is found, and keep cwd resolution otherwise; add a worktree test case.
- **Risk — filesystem scan cost per tick.** Mitigated by process-lifetime
  memoisation (AC 6) and by only scanning on a resolver cache miss.
- **Risk — test flakiness on timing.** The latency assertion (AC 4) could be
  environment-sensitive; pin it as a generous upper bound (e.g. ≤5 s) or measure
  the resolver's own budget rather than wall clock on a shared machine.
- **Scope-creep watch (linked follow-ups, not part of this change):** caching
  titles in the footer across sessions; showing status/priority in the footer;
  resolving multiple IDs in one command; surfacing a "not found" hint on
  failure. Record as separate work items if wanted.
- **Interpretation of "has stopped":** git history shows no regression — the
  cross-project gap predates the feature's original implementation. Documented
  here so the fix is not mis-scoped as a revert.

## Related work

- **WL-0MQLG8PK80041FM3** — Resolve work item IDs to titles in activity indicator
  footer (completed): introduced the resolution path and its graceful-fallback AC.
- **WL-0MQLJU82A000AT2W** — Preserve command context when showing resolved work
  item title in activity footer (completed): introduced `{command} {id} {title}`.
- **WL-0MRFH8W4J007HIY5** — Fix extractInitialPrompt to handle Pi's array-based
  content format (completed): added the line-3 initial-prompt title enrichment.
- **WL-0MUL1BG09005VRBO** — stale-ctx hardening of async paths (completed):
  guarded the post-await `showActivity` call; behaviour-neutral for this bug.
- **WL-0MRFOJFVA003S8IB** — Compact footer status line (completed): introduced
  `truncateWorkItemId` used in the composed footer label.
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — reference prefix-to-sibling resolver.
- `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — worklog-dir resolution
  background.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

### Original report (verbatim, producer)

> The Pi extension has stopped showing the item title in the footer. This doesn't
> always happen, only with some work items. It always shows the work item ID, but
> it should show the footer too. For example: /intake RISE-0MVCFSM9B0019M8L

No interview round was required: the report names the surface (footer), the
symptom (ID shown, title absent), and a concrete reproduction (`RISE-…`), and the
repo/CLI investigation below resolved the cause without needing producer input.

- **Q (interpretation, not asked):** does "it should show the footer too" mean
  the title should also appear? — **Assumed answer:** yes; the observed symptom is
  that the ID appears without the title, so the missing artefact is the title.
  Source: report text + reproduction. Status: **OPEN QUESTION** — see Research
  notes; the producer should confirm during review.

### Research notes

- **Duplicate check:** `wl search "Pi extension footer title"` and
  `wl search "extension title"` were run. The three completed items above overlap
  on the *feature* but none covers cross-project resolution or the timeout — this
  item is scoped to the gap, not a duplicate. No overlapping **open** item found.
- **Reproduction evidence:** `wl show RISE-0MVCFSM9B0019M8L --json` fails with
  "Work item not found" from ContextHub and succeeds from `tce-the-rising`.
  `tce-the-rising/.worklog/config.yaml` contains `prefix: RISE`.
- **Latency evidence:** cold `wl show RISE-0MVCFSM9B0019M8L --json` took 2.36 s
  for an 18 477-byte payload (budget in code: 2 000 ms); warm runs 1.10–1.29 s.
- **Git archaeology:** `git log -S "worklog-dir" -- packages/tui/extensions/wl-integration.ts`
  returns nothing — the extension never passed a worklog dir. Commit `9bc24414`
  (stale-ctx hardening) only wrapped the post-await call in `try/catch` and is
  behaviour-neutral. Commit `386ba9a2` deleted `activity-indicator.test.ts`,
  leaving the resolution path untested.
- **Plan-review open question — ambiguous prefixes:** how should the resolver
  behave when several sibling projects declare the same `prefix:` (e.g. `POD` ×
  12)? **Preferred option (recommended default):** verify ownership before
  accepting a candidate — prefer the candidate whose `.worklog/worklog.db`
  contains the ID (read-only existence check, cached per prefix→id), otherwise
  return `null` and fall back to cwd so no wrong title is ever displayed.
  **Alternative:** return `null` whenever a prefix is ambiguous (simpler, but
  `POD` items then never show a title in the footer). Why it matters: without a
  rule, AC 1 can pass for `RISE` while `POD` items resolve to the wrong project.
  Evidence: `for f in /home/rgardler/projects/*/.worklog/config.yaml` shows
  `POD` declared by 12 projects, `RISE` by one (`tce-the-rising`).
- **Open question (for producer review):** the report's phrase "it should show
  the footer too" is ambiguous — this brief assumes it means the **title** should
  also appear, which matches the observed symptom (ID shown, title absent). If
  the producer meant something else (e.g. a specific footer line disappearing),
  the diagnosis should be revisited.

## One-line headline summary

Work-item title resolution in the Pi extension footer silently fails for IDs that
live in a sibling project's worklog (e.g. `RISE-…`) and can time out on large
items; fix it by reusing the skills layer's prefix-to-sibling worklog resolution
in a single shared, memoised resolver for both footer call sites.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MRMG8P2X004V6YC** – help line for chord commands too verbose (completed)
- **WL-0MTF5WNRB009RHRU** – Pane-title: ID survives truncation, drop 'triggered' (completed)
- **WL-0MRDRZ32L00404D0** – Session Health Extension for Pi Footer (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: always, example, extension, footer, happen (+7 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: always, extension, footer, happen, intake (+5 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: always, example, extension, happen, intake (+5 more)

# Decompose the `worklist.ts` god class

**File:** `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — 7,823 lines, 89 exported symbols,
20 banner-delimited sections, one 2,260-line function (`runWorklistTui`, 5564–7823).

## Problem statement

`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` carries the entire Herdr work-item selection
experience — constants and maps, the mutable list state machine, row/detail/meta
formatting, tooltip and help rendering, chord and key handling, the mouse input
pipeline, the list renderer, command dispatch and the TUI lifecycle loop — in a
single 7,823-line module. Because the biggest single concern (`runWorklistTui`,
2,260 lines of nested closures over one large mutable context) sits in the same
file as everything else, every change requires holding thousands of unrelated
lines in view, and the blast radius of a diff is not legible from the file it
touches.

This item is the follow-up filed by WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 (producer directive,
intake Q1 → A: *"If any file is >1000 lines it should be evaluated for
refactoring and if appropriate a work item should be created"*). The
downtime-worker decomposition established the pattern this item reuses:
move-only extraction, thin compatibility barrel, tests untouched as the
behaviour gate, sequenced child items.

## Users

- **Herdr UI maintainers (agents and humans)** changing one concern (a key
  binding, the metadata panel, the mouse drag path, the refresh loop) without
  re-reading 7,800 lines.
- **Reviewers/auditors** who need a diff whose blast radius is attributable to
  one module and one test file.
- **Future agents** implementing worklist work items, who need named modules
  locatable by file search instead of a monolith.
- **Operators** who benefit indirectly: smaller modules shorten the review and
  audit cycle for every worklist change.

Example user stories:

- As an agent changing the metadata panel, I want `formatMetadataPanel` and its
  helpers in their own module so that I can verify the change against its own
  tests.
- As a reviewer, I want the key-handling diff to touch only the key-handling
  module so that I can reason about input regressions in isolation.
- As a maintainer, I want every module under 1,000 lines so that any one concern
  is readable in a single pass.
- As a maintainer, I want `runWorklistTui` to be a thin orchestrator over named
  handler modules so that the TUI lifecycle is reviewable.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No production file exceeds 1,000 lines.** After the change, `wc -l` reports
   ≤1,000 for `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (reduced to a thin barrel) and for
   every module created by the split. The single 2,260-line `runWorklistTui`
   function is broken up so no module and no single exported function carries it
   whole.
2. **Public surface preserved — used symbols only.** Every symbol currently
   imported from `./worklist.js` by another module remains exported from that
   exact path with identical types and values, so the 34 importing files
   (2 production consumers + 32 test files, of which 22 are `worklist*.test.ts`
   suites) compile with no import-path edits. 66 distinct symbols are imported
   today; the barrel
   re-exports **only symbols consumers actually use** — unused exports stay
   internal to the extracted modules (inherited producer decision, parent
   WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 intake Q2 → "A, but only re-export symbols that are
   actually used").
3. **Behaviour-preserving, move-only refactor.** No functional or logic change,
   no renames of public symbols, no behavioural diffs. No test file is modified —
   not its import paths, fixtures or assertions — and all 22 `worklist*.test.ts`
   suites (15,433 lines) plus the whole `packages/herdr` suite pass unchanged.
4. **No new circular imports.** Extracted modules import only from concrete
   sibling modules, never from the `worklist.js` barrel or from `index.ts`; the
   existing `worklist → fetcher/visibility/…` edge direction is preserved and no
   new cycle is introduced.
5. **State ownership is explicit and singular.** The mutable
   `WorkItemListState` (848-line section) and the TUI-local mutable context
   currently closed over by `runWorklistTui` each live in exactly one module;
   extraction must not duplicate mutable state or fork the source of truth.
6. **Responsibility documented per module.** Each new module carries a
   module-level doc comment stating its single responsibility, and existing
   provenance comments (work-item ids, section banners such as
   `// ── Mouse / touch input (WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ) ──`) move with their code so
   traceability is preserved.
7. **Testing/validation criterion:** the extracted modules are covered by the
   existing, unmodified `worklist*.test.ts` suites; the split adds no behaviour
   of its own, so no new assertions are required. Validation includes
   `tsc --noEmit`/build success, no new circular-import report, and a line-count
   check asserting every `packages/herdr/src/worklist*.ts` production module is
   ≤1,000 lines.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Move-only.** Relocate code and rewire imports; do not refactor logic,
  improve naming, or "fix" anything encountered on the way (record such findings
  as new work items instead).
- **Barrel compatibility.** 34 files import from `./worklist.js` or
  `./worklist` (including 22 `worklist*.test.ts` suites and the production
  consumers `index.ts` and `fetcher.ts`). The barrel preserves that contract.
- **Sequenced, tree-green landing.** Extract leaf modules first (constants,
  types, layout, formatting) and work inwards towards the state machine and the
  TUI loop, so each merged step leaves the build and the full suite green.
- **`runWorklistTui` is the hard part.** Its 2,260 lines are nested closures
  sharing one large mutable context. The extraction must keep a single context
  object (interface-typed, owned by one module) and pass it explicitly to
  extracted handler functions rather than duplicating state or converting to a
  class-based controller (that would be a behavioural rewrite, not a move).
- **No new runtime dependencies**, no test-file rewrites, no changes to Herdr
  key bindings, shortcuts, rendering output or the `wl` CLI contract.
- **Scope boundary.** This epic targets production modules under
  `packages/herdr/src/worklist*.ts`. Test files exceeding the ceiling
  (`worklist.test.ts` 7,073 lines, `worklist-mouse.test.ts` 1,132 lines) are
  **out of scope** under the recommended option (see Appendix Q1) and would be
  filed as a follow-up item, because splitting them would violate AC3
  (unmodified tests as the behaviour gate).
- **Other >1,000-line herdr files are out of scope** (tracked separately:
  `index.ts` WL-0MVGKGFFN009UCM6, `fetcher.ts` WL-0MVGKH47T007GKN1,
  `dispatcher-anchor.ts` WL-0MVGKHCP9005SJPZ, `downtime-log.ts`
  WL-0MVGKHFT4003X6JW, `downtime-worker.ts` WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7).

## Existing state

`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` is 7,823 lines, 89 exports, 20 sections (line
ranges from the current `dev` checkout):

| # | Section banner | Lines | Size | Exports |
|---|----------------|-------|------|---------|
| — | Header, JSDoc, imports | 1–90 | 90 | — |
| 1 | Input-active predicate (WL-0MTV67MZU003H7SH) | 91–160 | 70 | 2 |
| 2 | Constants | 161–185 | 25 | 3 |
| 3 | `/wl <stage>` argument map | 186–202 | 17 | 1 |
| 4 | `/wl --priority` map | 203–222 | 20 | 2 |
| 5 | Metadata panel sizing | 223–313 | 91 | 4 |
| 6 | Terminal helpers | 314–366 | 53 | 3 |
| 7 | Navigation Stack | 367–443 | 77 | 2 |
| 8 | State (`WorkItemListState`) | 444–1291 | 848 | 5 |
| 9 | Stage filter helper | 1292–1322 | 31 | 1 |
| 10 | Formatting functions | 1323–1618 | 296 | 2 |
| 11 | Hover tooltip rendering | 1619–1855 | 237 | 3 |
| 12 | Compound metadata rows | 1856–1918 | 63 | 1 |
| 13 | Description preview cache / metadata panel | 1919–2456 | 538 | 8 |
| 14 | Note-edit write-back + detail content | 2457–2708 | 252 | 6 |
| 15 | Chord state helpers | 2709–3193 | 485 | 9 |
| 16 | Keyboard handling | 3194–3522 | 329 | 4 |

  Everything else importing is a test.
- **`runWorklistTui` internal concerns** (from its nested-function scan):
  pane markers and event subscriptions (5606–6141), metadata blocker resolution
  (5654–5803), refresh/sync/dispatch (6143–6480), key input (6484–7172),

  `shortcut-config`, `auto-sync`, `scheduler`, `settings`, `db-change`,
  `downtime-worker`, `downtime-log`, `dispatch-view`, `hydrator`, `notify`,

Reduce `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` to a thin re-export barrel and move its

following decomposition is a **starting point** — boundaries are an

- **Risk — `runWorklistTui` closure extraction (high).** 2,260 lines of closures

## Decompose the `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` god module

**File:** `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` (2,935 lines, 37 exported symbols)

## Problem statement

`packages/herdr/src/index.ts` is the Herdr plugin entry point and has grown to
2,935 lines. It currently carries command routing, argument builders, background
dispatch, pane-ID capture, claim/priority resolution, interactive window and tab
placement, pane cleanup, dozens of production dependency resolvers, the
downtime-worker dependency factory, settings bootstrap and the full TUI
`main()` loop in one module. Navigating, reviewing and safely changing any one
concern requires holding the whole file in view, so every dispatch or TUI change
carries avoidable regression risk.

The 1,000-line maintainability ceiling was adopted for the parent refactor
series WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7. This item is the `index.ts` member of that sweep and
was created specifically to bring this file under the ceiling.

## Users

- **Herdr plugin maintainers (agents and humans)** need to change one concern
  (e.g. background dispatch, interactive placement, the TUI loop) without
  reasoning about 2,800 unrelated lines.
- **Reviewers/auditors** need a focused diff whose blast radius is legible from
  the touched module.
- **Future agents implementing plugin work items** need small, named modules
  they can locate with a file search instead of reading a monolith.

Example user stories:

- As an agent implementing a background-dispatch change, I want that path in a
  dedicated module so I can modify it without re-reading the TUI loop.
- As a reviewer, I want a split diff attributable to a single concern so I can
  verify it against its own tests.
- As a maintainer, I want each module under 1,000 lines so a file is readable in
  a single pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **No file exceeds 1,000 lines.** After the change, `wc -l` reports ≤1,000 for `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` (now a thin barrel/entry module) and for every module created by the split.
- **Public surface preserved — used symbols only.** Every symbol currently imported from `./index.js` by another module remains exported from that exact path with identical types and values, so `index.test.ts`, `claim.test.ts`, `fetchAuditItemById.test.ts` and `start.ts` compile with no import-path edits. The barrel re-exports **only symbols that are actually used** by consumers; unused exports stay internal to the extracted modules (inherited producer decision Q2 on the parent item, WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7).
- **Entry-point behaviour preserved.** `start.ts` dynamically imports `./index.js` and calls `main()`; `index.ts` keeps exporting `main` and keeps the `isEntryPoint` guard so importing the module in a vitest worker still does not launch the TUI or call `process.exit`. The entry guard stays in the entry module (not in an extracted helper) so `process.argv[1]` identity checks keep their current meaning.
- **Behaviour-preserving, move-only refactor.** No functional or logic change; no test file is modified (not its import paths, fixtures or assertions), and all `packages/herdr` test suites pass unchanged.
- **Module-level singletons stay singular.** The `const settings = loadSettings()` side effect (currently line 2246) is evaluated **exactly once** at module load and shared by `createDowntimeDeps` and `main()`. It must not be duplicated into two modules, or the plugin would load settings twice with potentially different results. The same rule applies to the resolved script paths (`SEND_TO_PI_SCRIPT`, `RUN_IN_PANE_SCRIPT`) which depend on `import.meta.url` staying in `packages/herdr/src/`.
- **No new circular imports.** Extracted modules import only from concrete sibling modules, never from the `index.js` barrel; the barrel imports downward only. The dependency check reports no new cycles (including the existing `stalled-work ↔ downtime-worker` type-only cycle, which must not be widened).
- **Responsibility documented per module.** Each new module carries a module-level doc comment stating its single responsibility, and existing provenance comments (work-item ids, section banners) move with their code so traceability is preserved.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes, and `npm run build` (tsc) must succeed — a module move that breaks the build is not a valid intermediate state.
## Constraints

- **Move-only.** Relocate code and update imports; do not refactor logic, rename
  public symbols, or change behaviour.
- **Barrel compatibility.** 3 test files and `start.ts` import from
  `./index.js`; the barrel preserves that contract (AC2/AC3).
- **Sequenced, tree-green landing.** Extract leaf modules first and work inwards,
  so each merged step leaves the build and the full suite green.
- **No new runtime dependencies**, no test-file rewrites, no changes to the wl
  CLI contract or to plugin behaviour.
- **Scope boundary.** This item targets `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` only. Test
  file size (`index.test.ts` is 3,990 lines), sibling production files and a
  repo-wide lint rule are out of scope (see Risks — scope creep).

## Existing state

`index.ts` is 2,935 lines. Its cohesive sections (line ranges from the current
`dev` checkout; updated by the plan session 2026-10-25) are:

| # | Section | Lines | Size |
|---|---------|-------|------|
| 1 | Header, imports and resolved script paths | 1–197 | 197 |
| 2 | Command routing + arg builders (`routeCommand`, `stripCommandPrefix`, `buildSendToPiArgs`, `buildRunInPaneArgs`, `parsePaneIdFile`) | 198–388 | 191 |
| 3 | Background (no-pane) dispatch (`BACKGROUND_LOG_DIR`, log helpers, `spawnBackgroundShell`, `spawnBackgroundPi`) | 389–602 | 214 |
| 4 | Pane-ID capture + work-item extraction (`CAPTURE_*`, `capturePaneIdFromFile`, `extractWorkItemId`) | 603–716 | 114 |
| 5 | Claim + interactive priority (`claimItemForAgentCommand`, `resolveInteractiveDispatchPriority`, priority lookup, critical blockers) | 717–817 | 101 |
| 6 | Default anchor resolvers (dispatcher/project/tab/item, internal) | 818–918 | 101 |
| 7 | Interactive placement + root-pane cleanup (`resolveInteractiveWorkspaceId`, `resolveInteractiveItemAnchor`, `closeInteractiveTabRootPane`, `defaultInteractiveLiveTrackedPanesResolver`, `defaultInteractiveClosePane`) | 919–1134 | 216 |
| 8 | Downtime/stalled resolvers (`defaultRunningDowntimePanesResolver`, `defaultStalledResume*`, `defaultStalledPanesLister`, `worklogRootFromPiSessionPath`, `defaultStalledPaneRootResolver`, `readClosedPaneIds`) | 1135–1345 | 211 |
| 9 | Host-CPU sampler (WL-0MVK0UO3Q002TXW6: `defaultHostCpuSampler`, `setHostCpuSamplerForTests`) | 1346–1400 | 55 |
| 10 | `createDowntimeDeps` dependency factory | 1401–2357 | 957 |

- **Used public surface (26 symbols):** static imports from `./index.js` are
  `stripCommandPrefix`, `routeCommand`, `stripAgentPromptPrefix`,
  `buildSendToPiArgs`, `buildRunInPaneArgs`, `createDowntimeDeps`,
  `capturePaneIdFromFile`, `parsePaneIdFile`, `buildBackgroundLogPath`,

  `CAPTURE_TIMEOUT_MS`, `extractWorkItemId`, `defaultStalledPaneRootResolver`,
  `defaultStalledPanesLister`, `worklogRootFromPiSessionPath`,
  `resolveInteractiveDispatchPriority`, `claimItemForAgentCommand`; dynamic

  `defaultInteractiveLiveTrackedPanesResolver`, `resolveInteractiveWorkspaceId`,
  `resolveInteractiveItemAnchor`, `closeInteractiveTabRootPane`; `start.ts`

- **Unused exported symbols (safe to keep internal):** `CommandRoute`,
  `BACKGROUND_LOG_DIR`, `BackgroundSpawnDeps`, `CAPTURE_POLL_INTERVAL_MS`,
  `PaneIdFileDeps`, `InteractiveLiveTrackedPanesResult`,
  `InteractiveRootPaneCleanupDeps`, `defaultInteractiveClosePane`,
  `defaultRunningDowntimePanesResolver`, `defaultStalledResumePromptAgent`,
  `defaultStalledResumeStartAgent`.
- **Single module-level side effect:** `const settings = loadSettings()` at line
  2246, read by `createDowntimeDeps` (line 2237) and `main()`. No other top-level
  statements exist beyond the entry guard.
- **Entry point chain:** `herdr-plugin.toml` launches
  `npx tsx src/start.ts`; `start.ts` dynamically imports `./index.js` and calls

- **Test gate:** `index.test.ts` (3,990 lines), `claim.test.ts` (407), and

- **Precedent:** WL-0MQJK4UJD0028IRO decomposed the 2,584-line

## Desired change

Reduce `index.ts` to a thin re-export barrel plus the entry-point guard and
shared bootstrap side effect, and move its contents into cohesive sibling
modules. A starting decomposition (boundaries are an implementation decision,
subject to the constraints above):

|---|---|---|
| `index.commands.ts` | `routeCommand`, `stripCommandPrefix`, `buildSendToPiArgs`, `buildRunInPaneArgs`, `parsePaneIdFile` and command-prefix helpers | ~210 |
| `index.background.ts` | Background (no-pane) dispatch: log paths, failure formatting, `spawnBackgroundShell`, `spawnBackgroundPi` | ~205 |

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**Inherited from the parent item (WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7) — no new questions
blocking:**

- Q (scope): Is the "no file > 1,000 lines" goal limited to this file, or should

  scan of `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`.
- Q: How many consumers depend on its public surface? — Answer: 3 test files
  (`index.test.ts`, `claim.test.ts`, `fetchAuditItemById.test.ts`) and

- Q: Is there module-level mutable state that a split could duplicate? — Answer:

- Q: What is the entry-point contract? — Answer: `herdr-plugin.toml` launches

  `packages/herdr/herdr-plugin.toml`, `packages/herdr/src/start.ts`,

**Plan session (2026-10-25):**

# Refactor: decompose `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` god class

## Problem statement

`packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` is 2,340 lines and holds a single
`SqlitePersistentStore` class spanning at least eight unrelated concerns
(connection open/read-only handling, schema DDL and additive repair, metadata
and delta-sync watermarks, work-item CRUD with hierarchy ordering, comment
CRUD, dependency-edge CRUD, audit-result CRUD, FTS5 index/search, and an
in-memory query cache). It breaches the 1,000-line maintainability ceiling
adopted for WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 and is hard to navigate, review and change
safely.

## Users

- **Agents implementing work items** — need to locate one concern (e.g. the FTS
  search path) without loading 2,340 unrelated lines into context.
- **Reviewers / producers auditing changes** — need a diff whose blast radius
  is legible from the touched module.
- **Operators / maintainers debugging storage behaviour** — need the read-only
  open contract, cache invalidation rules and FTS fallback readable in
  isolation.

Example user stories:

- As an agent, I want the FTS search/fallback logic in its own module, so that
  a change to ranking does not require reading schema, audit and comment code.
- As a reviewer, I want each extracted module to declare a single
  responsibility, so that I can judge a diff against one boundary.
- As a maintainer, I want `SqlitePersistentStore`'s public surface unchanged, so
  that `packages/shared/src/database.ts` and the benchmark consumers need no
  edits.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Ceiling met.** `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` and every file
   under `packages/shared/src/persistent-store/` is ≤ 1,000 lines (target:
   largest extracted module ≤ 600). Verified with pre/post `wc -l` output
   recorded on the work item.
2. **Public surface preserved.** `SqlitePersistentStore`,
   `PersistentStoreServices`, `PersistentStoreCacheOptions`,
   `PersistentStoreOpenOptions`, `FtsSearchResult`, `LastExportTimestamps`,
   `MigrationInfo`, `normalizeSqliteValue`, `normalizeSqliteBindings`,
   `unescapeText` and `parseAuditWaiver` remain importable from the unchanged
   specifiers `./persistent-store.js` (package build `dist/persistent-store.js`)
   with identical types and behaviour. Consumers —
   `packages/shared/src/database.ts` and `scripts/benchmark-caching.ts` — need
   no import-path edits.
3. **Move-only, behaviour-preserving.** No logic, SQL, ordering, error-message,
   schema, cache-semantics or public-signature change. No existing test file is
   modified (import paths, fixtures or assertions); all
   `packages/shared/src/*.test.ts` suites and the full project suite pass
   unchanged.
4. **No circular imports.** The extracted-module import graph is acyclic; no
   module imports the `persistent-store.ts` façade. Shared internal state
   (`db` handle, cache, SQL-binding helpers, row mappers) is reached through an
   internal context type, not by modules importing the façade.
5. **Responsibilities documented.** Each new module carries a header comment
   stating its single responsibility; `packages/shared/README.md` (Package
   Structure) lists the new layout.
6. **Builds and tests.** `npm run build:shared`, `npm run build` and the full
   project test suite pass (run through the test skill, not ad-hoc commands).
7. **Documentation updated.** All related documentation reflects the changes,
   including code comments, `packages/shared/README.md`, `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md`,
   `docs/design/incremental-sync.md`, `docs/dev/sync-persist-performance.md` and
   `docs/dev/wal-checkpointing-investigation.md` where they name this file as the
   home of a concern.

## Constraints

- **Move-only.** Extraction and relocation only; no "while we're here"
  rewrites. Method-level decomposition of any oversized method is allowed only
  where required to keep an extracted file under the ceiling, and lands as a
  separate commit from the pure move.
- **Barrel compatibility.** `persistent-store.ts` stays as the public entry,
  re-exporting the full current export set (11 symbols). It is not in the
  package `exports` map, but `packages/shared/src/database.ts` and
  `scripts/benchmark-caching.ts` (`dist/persistent-store.js`) resolve it by
  path, so the file must remain.
- **Package layout.** New modules live under
  `packages/shared/src/persistent-store/`, mirroring the `src/database/`
  layout agreed for the sibling epic WL-0MVGKGHNR0019OLT. `tsconfig` already
  includes `src/**/*`, so no build-config change is required.
- **Serialise with WL-0MVGKGHNR0019OLT** (`packages/shared/src/database.ts`) —
  same package and build; running both decompositions concurrently would churn
  `packages/shared/dist` and invite merge conflicts. Do not run both at once.
- **Scope boundary.** Only `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts`. The root
  sibling `src/persistent-store.ts` (1,653 lines) has its own item
  (WL-0MVGKGU19004NTHB) and is **out of scope**; the two files are divergent
  forks (the shared copy adds read-only open, audit-waiver parsing, the query
  cache and delta-sync watermarks), so no cross-file unification is attempted
  here.
- **No new runtime dependencies.** No changes to the wl CLI contract, storage
  schema, or the `@worklog/shared` package `exports` map.
- **Escaped backticks** only in written content; Markdown otherwise.

## Existing state

- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — 2,340 lines, 11 exports.
- Consumers (all resolve the same barrel path): `packages/shared/src/database.ts`
  imports `SqlitePersistentStore`, `FtsSearchResult`,
  `PersistentStoreServices`, `PersistentStoreCacheOptions`,
  `LastExportTimestamps`, `unescapeText`;
  `scripts/benchmark-caching.ts` dynamically imports
  `dist/persistent-store.js` for `SqlitePersistentStore`. No other source file
  imports the module directly.
- In-lockstep tests: `packages/shared/src/database.test.ts` (839),
  `dirty-tracking.test.ts` (384), `database-dedup.test.ts` (134),
  `audit-fingerprint-repair.test.ts` (135), `database-readonly.test.ts` (185)
  — all under 1,000 and exercise `SqlitePersistentStore` through
  `WorklogDatabase`. No test file needs splitting.
- Current section inventory (from the `dev` checkout):

| Section | Lines | Size |
|---|---|---|
| Module doc, interfaces, SQL-binding/waiver utilities | 1–258 | 258 |
| Constructor, connection open, read-only handling, schema init/repair | 259–594 | 336 |
| Metadata, last-export timestamps, delta-sync metadata | 595–705 | 111 |
| Work-item CRUD, sort-index and hierarchy ordering | 706–1186 | 481 |
| Comment CRUD | 1187–1287 | 101 |
| Dependency edges, `importData`, transactions | 1288–1449 | 162 |
| Audit results (`saveAuditResult`, `reconcileAuditInvalidation`, CRUD) | 1450–1667 | 218 |
| FTS5 index, `searchFts`, `searchFallback`, `findByIdSubstring` | 1668–2137 | 470 |
| In-memory cache helpers and invalidation | 2138–2230 | 93 |
| `close()` and row mappers (`rowToWorkItem`/`rowToComment`/`rowToDependencyEdge`) | 2231–2340 | 110 |

- **Sibling duplication relationship (investigated).** `src/persistent-store.ts`
  (1,653 lines) is an older fork of the same class: it lacks the shared copy's
  read-only open mode (`PersistentStoreOpenOptions`), `auditWaiver` column and
  `parseAuditWaiver`, the in-memory query cache (`PersistentStoreCacheOptions`),
  delta-sync watermarks (`LastExportTimestamps`,
  `getDeltaSyncMetadata`/`setDeltaSyncMetadata`) and
  `reconcileAuditInvalidation`. They are not interchangeable; leave both in
  place and refactor each under its own item.
- **Prior related attempt.** WL-0MQJK4UF0002OKUD ("Extract concerns from
  `SqlitePersistentStore`") touched the **root** `src/persistent-store.ts` on a
  feature branch only — none of its extracted modules
  (`src/lib/sql-bindings.ts`, `src/lib/fts-search.ts`,
  `src/lib/schema-manager.ts`) exist in the current tree. It is precedent for
  the decomposition shape, not a completed change to this file.
- **Precedent (same package).** WL-0MVGKGHNR0019OLT (in progress,
  `intake_complete`) decomposes `packages/shared/src/database.ts` (3,684 lines)
  into `packages/shared/src/database/*` behind an unchanged façade; this item
  follows the same layout and AC pattern and must be serialised with it.

## Desired change

Reduce `persistent-store.ts` to a thin façade/barrel that constructs the
collaborators and delegates, moving the method bodies into cohesive siblings
under `packages/shared/src/persistent-store/`. A starting map (boundaries are an
implementation decision, subject to the constraints above; every current method
belongs to exactly one row):

| Module | Responsibility | Est. lines |
|---|---|---|
| `persistent-store.ts` (façade) | Constructor, connection open (incl. read-only), `close()`, `ftsAvailable`/`readOnly` getters, delegation, barrel re-exports | ~300 |
| `persistent-store/types.ts` | `MigrationInfo`, `PersistentStoreServices`, `FtsSearchResult`, `PersistentStoreOpenOptions`, `LastExportTimestamps`, `PersistentStoreCacheOptions`, `DbMetadata`, `RequiredColumn`, `CacheEntry` | ~190 |
| `persistent-store/sql-bindings.ts` | `normalizeSqliteValue`, `normalizeSqliteBindings`, `unescapeText`, `parseAuditWaiver` | ~75 |
| `persistent-store/schema.ts` | `SCHEMA_VERSION`, `REQUIRED_COLUMNS`, `initializeSchema`, `repairRequiredColumns`, `isSchemaInitialised`, `detectFtsAvailable` | ~260 |
| `persistent-store/metadata.ts` | `getMetadata`/`setMetadata`/`getAllMetadata`, last-export timestamps, delta-sync metadata | ~115 |
| `persistent-store/work-items.ts` | Work-item CRUD, `countWorkItems`, duplicate lookup, `batchUpdateSortIndices`, hierarchy ordering, `rowToWorkItem` | ~560 |
| `persistent-store/comments.ts` | Comment CRUD, `rowToComment` | ~115 |
| `persistent-store/edges.ts` | Dependency-edge CRUD, `importData`, `transaction`/`transactionImmediate`, `rowToDependencyEdge` | ~175 |
| `persistent-store/audit-results.ts` | Audit-result CRUD, `reconcileAuditInvalidation` | ~220 |
| `persistent-store/fts.ts` | `initializeFts`, `upsertFtsEntry`/`deleteFtsEntry`, `rebuildFtsIndex`, `searchFts`, `searchFallback`, `findByIdSubstring`, snippet helpers | ~470 |
| `persistent-store/cache.ts` | Cache get/set/invalidate helpers and mutation-scoped invalidators | ~105 |

Dependency direction after extraction: `persistent-store.ts` → {any module};
modules → `types.ts`, `sql-bindings.ts`, `../types.js`, `../status-stage-rules.js`,
`@worklog/shared/icons` and an internal context type. `fts.ts` may call
work-item/comment collaborators through the context; no module imports the
façade.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — reduce to façade + barrel; preserve all 11 exports.
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store/types.ts` — new; extracted interfaces.
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store/sql-bindings.ts` — new; binding/escape/waiver utilities.
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store/schema.ts` — new; DDL, versioning and additive repair.
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store/metadata.ts` — new; metadata and export/delta watermarks.
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store/work-items.ts` — new; item CRUD and ordering.
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store/comments.ts` — new; comment CRUD.
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store/edges.ts` — new; edge CRUD, import and transactions.
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store/audit-results.ts` — new; audit-result storage.
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store/fts.ts` — new; FTS5 index and search/fallback.
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store/cache.ts` — new; in-memory query cache.
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — verify unchanged (barrel contract).
- `packages/shared/README.md` — Package Structure section.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Circular imports via the façade (medium).** A module importing
  `./persistent-store.js` would cycle through the barrel. *Mitigation:* modules
  import concrete siblings plus an internal context type; the façade imports
  downward only. Enforced by AC4 and a static import scan (no
  `madge`/`dependency-cruiser` in the repo).
- **Shared `private` state (`db`, `_cache`, `_ftsAvailable`).** Nearly every
  method touches `this.db` and the cache invalidation helpers. *Mitigation:*
  inventory every `this.` access per method before moving; express it on an
  internal context (`StoreContext`) so extracted modules stay acyclic and
  testable.

  edits, especially in `saveWorkItem` (24-column upsert), hierarchy ordering and
  FTS ranking. *Mitigation:* move-only rule, unchanged test suite, and a review
  pass diffing moved blocks against the original.
- **Cache-semantics drift (medium).** `invalidateWorkItemCaches` clears several
  key families; splitting may drop one. *Mitigation:* keep all invalidators in

  `read-cache-prune` suites.
- **Build/packaging.** `scripts/benchmark-caching.ts` resolves
  `dist/persistent-store.js`; the façade must keep that exact output path (the
  `dist/persistent-store/` sibling directory coexists safely).
- **Merge contention with WL-0MVGKGHNR0019OLT.** *Mitigation:* serialise the
  two items; do not run both concurrently.
- **Assumption:** the 1,000-line ceiling applies to non-test source; no test
  file exceeds it here, so no test splitting is needed.
- **Assumption:** no consumer call-site changes are acceptable, including in
  `scripts/` and `bench/`.
- **Assumption:** no behavioural improvement is bundled in; anything observed
  en route becomes a separate `discovered-from` work item.
- **Scope-creep risk (explicit).** Unifying the two `persistent-store.ts`
  forks, adding a repo-wide file-length lint, refactoring `database.ts`, or
  reorganising cache behaviour are **out of scope** and must be recorded as
  linked follow-ups rather than absorbed here.

- **WL-0MVGKGHNR0019OLT** — sibling epic: decompose

  `docs/design/incremental-sync.md`, `docs/dev/sync-persist-performance.md`,
  `docs/dev/wal-checkpointing-investigation.md`, `packages/shared/README.md`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No producer interview questions were required: the seed context (goal, drafted
ACs, parent directive) plus repository inspection is sufficient to draft an
actionable brief, and every remaining choice is a reversible design decision
that plan/implement can adjust. The agent decisions below are recorded for
review, consistent with the sibling epic WL-0MVGKGHNR0019OLT.

- **Q: Does this item also cover the root `src/persistent-store.ts`?**
  **Answer (agent, by repository inspection): No.**
  Evidence: a dedicated item exists (WL-0MVGKGU19004NTHB), and the two files
  are divergent forks — the shared copy adds read-only open, audit-waiver

- **Q: Keep a barrel at `persistent-store.ts`, or update importers to the new
